explainedBy: A busy manager, the default corporate figure: a stack of paper and no time.

storyboard.claim: The narrator sets up a busy corporate manager.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manager in an office holding a sheet of paper.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the busy manager before the bowling set-up.
storyboard.staging: Manager with a sheet of paper and a worried face.

explainedBy: The manager sets up a bowling alley outing for the department.

storyboard.claim: The manager organises a bowling team-building outing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manager pointing down a bowling lane at an employee.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The office manager now sets up a bowling outing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the set-up in a bowling lane.
storyboard.staging: Manager points toward the lane, employee beside him.

explainedBy: The manager stretches a heavy canvas sheet across the lane to hide the pins.
noVisual: A bed sheet is not in the icon vocabulary; the callout carries it.

storyboard.claim: The manager hangs a canvas sheet across the bowling lane.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager reaching toward the lane where the sheet hangs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The team-building set-up becomes a blind game.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the sheet that hides the pins.
storyboard.staging: Manager reaches out as if hanging the sheet.

explainedBy: The employee cannot see the pins behind the sheet at all.

storyboard.claim: The sheet hides the pins from the bowler.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The employee at the lane, facing the sheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sheet is now hanging across the lane.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the blindness the narration describes.
storyboard.staging: Employee faces the blank sheet, worried.

explainedBy: The employee bowls blind: the ball disappears under the sheet.

storyboard.claim: The ball rolls under the sheet, out of sight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same employee at the lane, the ball gone under the sheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage: the bowl happens behind the sheet.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the ball going under the sheet.
storyboard.staging: Employee stands still, the ball out of view.

explainedBy: The employee hears pins fall but cannot tell how many.

storyboard.claim: The employee hears a crash but does not know the result.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The employee listening, uneasy, facing the sheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person, now reacting to the sound.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pins fell but the count is unknown.

explainedBy: The manager, hidden behind the sheet, peeks over it at the bowler.

storyboard.claim: The manager has been behind the sheet all along.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager's head above the sheet looking at the employee.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The employee is still blind; the manager now appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: The manager was behind the sheet with a clipboard.
storyboard.staging: Manager looks over the sheet at the employee.

explainedBy: The manager reveals the score by holding up two fingers: eight pins were missed.

storyboard.claim: The manager tells the employee he missed eight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager holds up two fingers over the sheet while the employee looks worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage: the manager now gives the verdict.
storyboard.staging: Manager points with two fingers; employee reacts worried.

explainedBy: The narrator names the absurdity of forcing employees to work this way every day.
noVisual: A commentary on work with no single person or object to stage.

storyboard.claim: The blind bowling set-up is absurd.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame: the callout carries the judgement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator steps back from the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Generalises the bowling image to daily work.
storyboard.staging: No person on screen; the callout speaks.

explainedBy: The manager waits months before telling the employee the mistake, at the annual review.

storyboard.claim: Feedback comes only at the annual review, months later.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock beside the manager, waiting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator explains the delay after the bowling scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: The delay is six months until review.
storyboard.staging: Clock with a manager waiting, blank face.

explainedBy: Legacy organisations run on this same default system.
noVisual: An abstract structural claim; no icon reads as an operating system.

storyboard.claim: Legacy organisations default to this blind-review structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame naming the default structure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator generalises to every legacy organisation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the bowling as a structure, not an accident.
storyboard.staging: No person; callout carries the claim.

explainedBy: Managing people is assumed to need a heavy, secret process run by one controlling person.

storyboard.claim: Managing people is assumed to require a secretive process.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manager controlling from behind the scene, shown by the puppeteer icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The default system is now described as secret control.
storyboard.addedInformation: The process is heavy and hidden.
storyboard.staging: Manager with a knowing smirk, puppeteer icon beside.

explainedBy: The manager holds all the cards while the employee is left guessing what success looks like.

storyboard.claim: The manager keeps the information; the employee guesses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager holding the notes; the employee beside him, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The default system becomes a relation between two people.
storyboard.addedInformation: The manager controls what success means.
storyboard.staging: Manager holds the notes, employee looks lost.

explainedBy: The narrator rejects the old assumption that managing needs secrecy.
noVisual: The rejection is a verbal claim; no object shows it.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the old assumption.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame: the struck-through callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A turn: the narrator says the assumption is wrong.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks the rejection of the premise.

explainedBy: The best tool is not hours of micromanaging, which the narrator rejects.

storyboard.claim: The best tool is not endless micromanagement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager pointing at the employee, who looks worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator rules out the usual tool.
storyboard.staging: Manager hovers over the employee, employee uneasy.

explainedBy: The ultimate tool is short, clear and honest moments with the employee.

storyboard.claim: The tool is short, clear, honest moments.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager talking in a calm, brief way.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator names the replacement tool.

explainedBy: Three distinct moments: a goal, a praise and a correction.

storyboard.claim: Three moments make up the method.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter diagram with three buckets: goal, praise, correction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator lists the three moments.

explainedBy: The narrator says the framework needs its context to be understood.
noVisual: A transition line; nothing to stage.

storyboard.claim: The framework needs context to understand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A transition into the story.

explainedBy: The young employee travels the world on a road, searching.

storyboard.claim: A young employee travels in search of a better way to lead.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee walking along a road.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The story begins: the protagonist is introduced.
storyboard.staging: Young man walks along the road.

explainedBy: The young employee searches for an effective boss, shown by the compass.

storyboard.claim: He searches for a truly effective boss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Young man walking with a compass icon beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The protagonist now has a search.
storyboard.addedInformation: The goal is a good boss.
storyboard.staging: Walking on the road with the compass.

explainedBy: Two management philosophies he keeps meeting.

storyboard.claim: Two dominant management types.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter diagram with two buckets: autocrats and participative managers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator names the two archetypes.

explainedBy: The tough autocrat commands and controls, and the employee shrinks before him.

storyboard.claim: The autocrat is a command-and-control boss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Angry manager pointing, the employee afraid beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first archetype: the autocrat.
storyboard.staging: Manager angry and pointing at the employee.

explainedBy: The autocrat cares only about results, not the people.

storyboard.claim: The autocrat cares only about the bottom line.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same angry manager pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage: the callout now names his priority.

explainedBy: The results come with burned-out, miserable people left behind.

storyboard.claim: The autocrat leaves burned-out people behind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager still pointing; the employee now sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cost lands on the employee.

explainedBy: The autocrat wins, but his people lose and talent leaves.

storyboard.claim: The autocrat wins; people lose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager neutral, the employee sad and slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The manager eases off; the human cost is shown.

explainedBy: The second archetype: the nice, participative manager at the other extreme.

storyboard.claim: The participative manager is the other extreme.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A warm manager beside the employee.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The second archetype begins.

explainedBy: The participative manager wants everyone to feel good and be loved.

storyboard.claim: The participative manager wants to be loved.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Happy manager with a heart icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The heart icon adds the wish to be loved.

explainedBy: The participative manager is too afraid to hold anyone accountable.

storyboard.claim: The participative manager fears accountability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager with a fearful face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fear behind the niceness.
storyboard.addedInformation: The organisation loses as a result.

explainedBy: Short-term win for people leads to the business failing and everyone losing jobs.

storyboard.claim: The participative approach ends with everyone losing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow diagram: people win, business fails, everyone loses.
storyboard.onScreenText: People win, business fails, everyone loses
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cause and effect of the nice approach.

explainedBy: The toxic idea: you must choose between a ruthless tyrant and a pushover.

storyboard.claim: The first false choice is the ruthless tyrant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Angry manager pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator returns to the choice.

explainedBy: The other option of the false choice: a beloved but ineffective pushover.

storyboard.claim: The second false choice is the beloved pushover.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Warm, ineffective manager.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The other half of the false choice.

explainedBy: The modern workplace runs on one metric: speed, with work done on a laptop.

storyboard.claim: Speed is the metric of the modern workplace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Young employee holding a laptop, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The protagonist lands in a modern workplace.

explainedBy: Decisions going up and back down the chain make the competitor win.

storyboard.claim: The old hierarchy is too slow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow diagram: decisions up the chain, back down, competitor wins.
storyboard.onScreenText: Decisions go up and back down the chain
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator explains why hierarchy fails.
storyboard.addedInformation: The competitor beats you to market.

explainedBy: Innovation happens at the edges, where he meets an unusual manager.

storyboard.claim: He meets a manager doing the impossible at the edge of the company.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Surprised employee facing the manager.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The protagonist meets the manager.
storyboard.addedInformation: The meeting point is the edge.

explainedBy: The manager gets incredible results while staying collaborative and hands-off.

storyboard.claim: This manager wins on results.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Happy manager with a trophy icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The new manager is introduced.

explainedBy: The manager works through precise, very short interventions, each about a minute.

storyboard.claim: The manager uses precise, short interventions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager talking, clock beside for one minute.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator introduces the method of the manager.
